language_wrapper: Inside a fixed regular {n}-gon (with vertices labeled cyclically 0 through {n_minus_1}), consider all rectangles whose sides each lie entirely on some side or diagonal of the polygon. Opposite sides of the rectangle must be parallel, and the two pairs of opposite sides must be perpendicular to each other. Additionally, impose the restriction that the two "horizontal" sides of the rectangle must lie on chords whose vertex-step sizes belong to the set {allowed_steps_h}, while the two "vertical" sides must lie on chords whose vertex-step sizes belong to the set {allowed_steps_v}. The vertex-step size of a chord is defined as the smaller number of edges traversed along the polygon from one endpoint to the other. Determine the number of such rectangles.
hardness_rationale: The core idea—counting rectangles in a regular polygon whose sides lie on sides or diagonals—persists. Difficulty increases because: (1) the polygon size is parametric (varied n divisible by 4), (2) rectangles are filtered by step-size restrictions for each perpendicular orientation, requiring careful categorization of chords by orientation classes modulo pi, and (3) correctness demands handling when endpoints coincide (vertex corners) and ensuring segment intersections rather than merely line intersections. The solver must combine orientation arithmetic (modular angle classes) with nontrivial combinatorial selection under constraints, exceeding the seed’s uniform dodecagon count.
notes: Implementation builds all chord segments in canonical form (minimal step direction), groups them by orientation id (computed as (2*a + d) mod n/2), and enumerates rectangles via unordered pairs in a perpendicular class pair, applying a robust segment-intersection test that includes shared-vertex intersections.
source_question: Find the number of rectangles that can be formed inside a fixed regular dodecagon ( $12$ -gon) where each side of the rectangle lies on either a side or a diagonal of the dodecagon. The diagram below shows three of those rectangles. [asy] unitsize(0.6 inch); for(int i=0; i<360; i+=30) { dot(dir(i), 4+black); draw(dir(i)--dir(i+30)); } draw(dir(120)--dir(330)); filldraw(dir(210)--dir(240)--dir(30)--dir(60)--cycle, mediumgray, linewidth(1.5)); draw((0,0.366)--(0.366,0), linewidth(1.5)); [/asy]
